questions.question_text: Which of these statements is true?

options.why: Added the numbers under the roots instead of multiplying them.
Applied the product rule to addition; the left side is $7$ but the right side is about $5.4$.
Applied the product rule to subtraction; the left side is $3$ but the right side is about $4.6$.

questions.question_text: Write $\sqrt{16}\times\sqrt{9}$ as a single square root.

options.why: Added the numbers under the roots instead of multiplying them.
Subtracted the numbers under the roots instead of multiplying them.
Multiplied $16\times 9$ and then squared the result before putting it under the root.
Added $\sqrt{4}$ and $\sqrt{25}$ instead of multiplying them.
Square rooted only the $25$ and multiplied the result by the whole $4$.
Multiplied the numbers under the root but did not take the square root at the end.
Divided $12$ by $3$ under the root instead of multiplying, giving $\sqrt{4}$.
Multiplied to get $\sqrt{36}$ then halved $36$ instead of taking its square root.
Multiplied the numbers under the roots but did not take the square root at the end.
Combined the two roots into $\sqrt{36+64}=\sqrt{100}$; the product rule does not hold for addition.
Multiplied the two square roots instead of adding them.
Added the numbers under the roots and took no square root at all.

questions.question_text:
What number goes in the box?
$\quad\sqrt{7}\times\sqrt{\square}=\sqrt{63}$

options.why: Gave $\sqrt{9}=3$ rather than the number that belongs under the root sign.
Subtracted $7$ from $63$ instead of dividing by $7$.
Multiplied $63$ by $7$ instead of dividing by $7$.
Square rooted only two of the three factors, leaving $\sqrt{4}$ out of the product.
Multiplied the three numbers to get $576$ and then halved it instead of square rooting.
Multiplied the numbers under the root but did not take the square root at the end.

questions.question_text:
A rectangle has width $\sqrt{6}$ cm and length $\sqrt{24}$ cm.
Find its area as a basic numeral.

options.why: Divided $24$ by $6$ under the root instead of multiplying, giving $\sqrt{4}$.
Added the numbers under the roots instead of multiplying them.
Multiplied the numbers under the roots but did not take the square root at the end.
